items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Then there was Carmite Thompson, who was a trumpet player out of Dallas, Texas.

ctx.x: Anyway, during my stay in Kansas City from -- let's see, '25 to '29, bands came through there such as the McKinney Cottonpickers, Zach Jack Whyte, Jack Allen's Cottonpickers, the Blues Serenaders, the Rice Brothers from Milwaukee, Zilver Randolph, who later I met in Chicago, in the '30s after I became a musician myself. However, I worked for him in Chicago.

Who else came through there? Oh. Barron Lee. It was a band out of, say, something like the Southern part of the South. I don't know exactly which state. Then there was Carmite Thompson, who was a trumpet player out of Dallas, Texas. He was a rather young man. And these bands I heard constantly, like, weekends on the domestics' nights off.

Then, we went back to Oklahoma in '29. And these same bands was coming through Oklahoma. And when I got to Oklahoma, I ran into the bands of Alphonso Trent, Clyde Love, no, Clarence Love, what's this other -- Tee Holder. And the local bands, which was two, one and two -- of course, there were others, but the number one band was Ernie Fields. And he had a trumpet player with him then -- this was like '31. And this kid was 21, and his father was a bandmaster and had a band of his own. His name was Fred Skinner. And…
